title: Variable-capacity cashflow smoothing and collection playbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook describes the operational procedures, decision thresholds, and accounting guidance for smoothing cashflow and managing collections for customers on variable-capacity contracts (metered usage, burst pools, or hybrid reserved + overage billing). It aligns procurement, contracting, billing ops, revenue recognition, and forecasting so that short-term cash disruptions from large usage swings are controlled while preserving customer relationships.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: provide standardized steps to minimize month-to-month cash volatility from variable-capacity customers and reduce days-sales-outstanding (DSO) for high-usage accounts.
- Scope: applies to all enterprise and MID-MARKET customers where monthly usage can exceed committed tiers by >25% in a single month. Excludes pure self-serve free-tier accounts unless flagged by finance ops.

Principles:
- Predictability first: prefer small, contractual monthly true-ups over ad-hoc large invoices.
- Risk-based controls: escalate highest-risk accounts earlier (PSA score >= 70, see Risk Scoring below).
- Customer-first collections: use graduated, account-managed contact before legal escalation.

Key stakeholders and ownership:
- Finance Ops (billing): owner for invoicing cadence, aging reports, and credit holds. Service: rwb-billing (internal microservice).
- Revenue Accounting: owner for RevRec entries and deferred revenue adjustments.
- Sales Ops / Account Executive: owner for customer communication and contract concessions.
- Procurement (customer side interface): coordinates escalation for large enterprise customers.
- Legal: sign-off for contract amendments > $250k MRR impact.

Risk Scoring (input to cadence):
- Usage volatility (30/90 day variance): >50% = 30 pts
- Outstanding balance / ARR ratio: >5% = 20 pts
- Payment history: 1 late pay in 12 months = 10 pts, 2+ = 25 pts
- Contractual dispute history: each dispute = 15 pts
- Total score >= 70 => High risk, 40-69 => Medium, <40 => Low.

Operational thresholds and SLOs:
- Invoice generation SLA: billing run must issue preliminary invoice within 72 hours of month close (owner: Finance Ops).
- True-up cadence for variable accounts: default monthly; optional biweekly when forecast delta > 30%.
- DSO target: 35 days company-wide; High-risk accounts target: <25 days.
- Credit hold threshold: unpaid aging > 45 days AND balance > $25k (except with AE exceptions).

Procedures (step-by-step):
1) Pre-close forecasting adjustment (day -5 relative to month close):
   - Finance Ops pulls usage signal from telemetry (service: rwb-usage-collector) and compares to committed tiers.
   - If projected overage > 25% of committed band, flag account and notify AE + Revenue Accounting.

2) Proactive mini-invoice offer (day -3):
   - For accounts with projected >50% overage, offer a biweekly invoice or interim true-up. AE negotiates options and signs in Salesforce (sf-opportunity ID appended to billing ticket).

3) Final invoice and allowances (day 0 to +3):
   - Issue final invoice in rwb-billing. Attach usage report CSV and reconciled mapping to contract line-items.
   - Revenue Accounting determines recognition split: immediate recognition for usage-billed items; deferred for prepayments per policy (see Accounting examples).

4) Collections cadence (post-invoice):
   - Day 1-14: automated payment retry (2 attempts) + first reminder email (Finance Ops).
   - Day 15-30: AE outreach + second reminder; account risk score recalculated.
   - Day 31-45: Senior AE + Finance Ops coordinated call; consider payment plan.
   - Day 46-60: Credit hold triggered if threshold met; notify Legal and Procurement contacts.
   - Day 61+: Legal collections and possible contract enforcement (requires Legal + Revenue Accounting sign-off).

Escalation matrix (owners and SLAs):
- Finance Ops: issue invoices and runage reports within 72h of close.
- AE: first personalized outreach within 7 days of overdue.
- Sales Ops: approve payment plans up to $100k and duration up to 90 days.
- Legal: approve escalation to collections for >$250k outstanding or repeated defaults.

Accounting guidance (examples):
- Scenario A: Metered overage invoice sent and paid within term:
  - Invoice creates AR at invoice date. Once cash collected: Debit Cash; Credit AR. Revenue recognized per usage delivered.
- Scenario B: Prepaid reserved pool with monthly true-up and credit applied:
  - On prepayment: Debit Cash; Credit Deferred Revenue. 
  - On monthly true-up (usage consumed): Debit Deferred Revenue; Credit Revenue (when performance obligation satisfied).
- Scenario C: Credit memo for billed dispute resolved in favor of customer:
  - Issue credit memo referencing invoice_id. Accounting: Debit Revenue (reversal); Credit AR/Cash depending on follow-up.

Example invoice timing table (recommended):
| Customer risk | Forecast delta | Suggested cadence | Credit policy |
| High         | >50%           | Biweekly or immediate true-up | Strict: hold >45d & >$25k |
| Medium       | 25-50%         | Monthly + optional interim | Moderate: hold >60d |
| Low          | <25%           | Monthly (standard)           | Standard: hold >90d |

Integration with forecasting and procurement:
- Forecasts must ingest committed capacity + rolling 90-day usage to generate cashflow curves. Finance Forecasting team will apply a smoothing algorithm (exponential smoothing with alpha=0.25 default) to produce the monthly cash impact used in run-rate forecasts.
- Procurement alignment: when a customer requests increased capacity, Sales Ops must issue a Capacity Change Request (CCR) that includes an updated procurement authorization and revised billing terms. CCRs > $250k ARR require procurement checklist and Legal review.

Monitoring, alerts, and dashboards:
- Dashboards (owner: Finance Analytics):
  - Monthly usage delta heatmap (by customer, product).
  - Aging buckets: 0-30,31-60,61-90,90+ with drilldown to AE.
  - Cashflow smoothing impact simulation panel.
- Alerts (owner: Finance Ops):
  - Usage spike alert: projected >100% month-over-month (severity P1).
  - Aging threshold breach: high-risk account hits 30 days overdue (severity P2).

Sample CLI snippets (internal tooling):
- Export usage for account 12345 for month:
  $ rwb-billing export-usage --account 12345 --month 2028-12 --format csv
- Create interim invoice:
  $ rwb-billing create-invoice --account 12345 --period 2028-12 --type interim --notify ae:jon.doe@example.com

Record retention and evidence for audits:
- Keep usage CSV, invoicing run log, AE email trail, and CCR approvals for a minimum of 7 years for enterprise customers. Evidence folder naming convention: /evidence/{account-id}/{year-month}/.

Appendix: common questions
Q: When do we move an account to reserved-only?
A: Consider reserved-only when an account’s monthly overage has occurred in 3 of 6 months and the ARR impact of reserving reduces expected unit cost by >15%. Sales Ops evaluates and drafts an amendment.

Q: Who approves discounts applied to interim invoices?
A: Discounts >10% must be approved by Head of Revenue (Finance + Sales sign-off).
